newsitem.title: CHINA: China may soon scatter ashes of Deng Xiaoping.
newsitem.headline: China may soon scatter ashes of Deng Xiaoping.

text.p: The family of Deng Xiaoping is expected to fulfil a last wish of the late paramount leader and scatter his ashes at sea very soon, an official at China Central Television (CCTV) said on Sunday.
"As soon as this happens, we expect to show the event on our evening news broadcast," said the official, who declined to be identified.
He refused to say when Deng's ashes would be scattered, or where, but said the private family event could take place "within these few days".

Hong Kong's TVB television station reported that Deng's family had left their home in central Beijing early on Sunday with the ashes of the man who ruled China for 18 years until his death on February 19 aged 92.
The family took the ashes to the Zhongnanhai government compound before leaving for a military airbase in a Beijing suburb, TVB reported.
It said his ashes were then flown to Shanghai where they would be taken aboard a naval vessel that would sail either to the East China Sea or the South China Sea.
The CCTV official confirmed that itinerary but refused to give a date.

The Hong Kong television station showed footage of a motorcade leaving Deng's home in a quiet alley behind the Forbidden City, home of China's emperors. Those inside the cars could be seen wearing white flowers, a symbol of mourning.
The motorcade was shown later leaving Zhongnanhai, where soldiers with white flowers pinned to their uniforms saluted as the cars drove away.
TVB said its reporters were barred from approaching the airbase in a western Beijing suburb, but a dirge could be heard playing for about 10 minutes before a plane took off.
Deng died of lung problems and complications from Parkinson's disease.
